`gsm.ctas` runs the [ctas](https://github.com/IMPALA-Consortium/ctas) clinical
trial anomaly detection engine inside the
[gsm](https://github.com/Gilead-Public/gsm.core) workflow framework and writes
the three files the
[ctasapp](https://github.com/IMPALA-Consortium/ctasapp) dashboard reads.

## Structure

### Functions

This package provides gsm-style functions to run `ctas` on SDTM formatted data view its output within `ctasapp` or to render an html report.

- `Standardize_Domain()`, `Standardize_Query` standardize data for ctas run
- `Transform_Missing()`, `Transform_Range()`, `Transform_OneHot()` transform non-standard numeric data types
- `Analyze_CTAS()` run `ctas`
- `BindResults_CTAS()`, `Summarize_CTAS()`, `Flag_CTAS()`, `MakeMetric_CTAS()`, `Report_CTAS()` reporting functions
- `Write_ctasapp()` write parquet files for `ctasapp` from reporting artifacts


### Workflow

- `inst/workflow/1_mappings` (data specification, filtering)
- `inst/workflow/2_metrics` (expect one yaml file per ctas configuration set, as different domains data types may require different ctas parameters, only average for one hot encoded data, custom timeseries for specific assessments)
- `inst/workflow/3_reporting` (create artifacts for `ctasapp` and html report)
- `inst/workflow/4_modules` (render html report)



## Installation

```{r inst, eval = FALSE}
install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("IMPALA-Consortium/gsm.ctas")
```



## Usage

`gsm.ctas` ships three gsm workflow layers in `inst/workflow/`, so a full run
is a sequence of `RunWorkflows()` calls over SDTM input:

```{r workflow, file = system.file("examples", "workflow.R", package = "gsm.ctas"), eval = FALSE}
```

### ctasapp

`ctasapp` needs to be installed and a ctasapp.yml needs to be present and entries need to point to parquet file.

```{r app, eval=FALSE}
Write_ctasapp(lReporting, strDir = ".", strFormat = "parquet")


# remotes::install_github("IMPALA-Consortium/ctasapp")
# file.copy(system.file("ctasapp.yml", package = "ctasapp"), "ctasapp.yml")
# embedded:
#   results: results.parquet
#   input: input.parquet
#   untransformed: untransformed.parquet
#   queries: queries.parquet
#   pd: pd.parquet

ctasapp::run_ctas_app()
```


### html Report

```{r report, eval=TRUE}
lModuleFlows <- workr::MakeWorkflowList(strPath = system.file("workflow/4_modules", package = "gsm.ctas"))

workr::RunWorkflows(
  lWorkflows = lModuleFlows,
  lData = lReporting
)
```


## Extending

new data fields can be added via the `1_mappings` workflows and need to be taken up in `2_metrics` for processing by either one of the exisiting configurations or by creating a new one. **One config file per ctas run parameter configuration**.


## Example

Score sites on a single numeric SDTM field (systolic blood pressure) using
only `gsm.ctas` functions, straight from raw SDTM to CTAS results:

```{r example}
library(gsm.ctas)

dfSubjects <- data.frame(
  studyid    = gsm.ctas::dm$STUDYID,
  subject_id = gsm.ctas::dm$USUBJID,
  site       = gsm.ctas::dm$SITEID,
  country    = gsm.ctas::dm$COUNTRY
)

dfInput <- Standardize_Domain(
  dfDomain     = subset(gsm.ctas::vs, VSTESTCD == "SYSBP"),
  dfSubjects   = dfSubjects,
  strTestCDCol = "VSTESTCD",
  strTestCol   = "VSTEST",
  strValueCol  = "VSSTRESN",
  strCategory  = "Vital Signs"
)

head(dfInput)

dfResults <- Analyze_CTAS(
  dfInput = dfInput,
  bAutocorr = TRUE,
  bAverage = TRUE,
  bSD = TRUE,
  bRange = FALSE,
  bUniqueValueCountRelative = TRUE,
  bOwnSiteSimilScore = FALSE,
  bLOF = FALSE,
  nMinTimepoints = 1,
  nMinSubjects = 3,
  dMaxShareMissing = 0.5,
  bChangeFromBaseline = FALSE,
  bAutogenerate = TRUE,
  strScoringMethod = "ks",
  strPadjustMethod = "fdr",
  dfCustomTimeseries = ctas::ctas_data$custom_timeseries,
  dfCustomReferenceGroups = ctas::ctas_data$custom_reference_groups,
  nSeed = 1,
  strStudyCol = "studyid"
)

head(dfResults)
```



## Contributing

Issues and pull requests are welcome. Please use the issue templates in
`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/` and see the
[Contributor Guidelines vignette](https://impala-consortium.github.io/gsm.ctas/articles/ContributorGuidelines.html)
for branch conventions, the development process, and the full list of
required CI checks.


## Quality Control

Since {gsm} is designed for use in a
[GCP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Good_clinical_practice) framework,
we have conducted extensive quality control as part of our development
process. In particular, we do the following during early development:

- **Unit Tests** - Unit tests are written for all core functions, 100%
  coverage required.
- **Workflow Tests** - Additional unit tests confirm that core workflows
  behave as expected.
- **Issue-Linked Tests** - Every GitHub issue is either linked to at least
  one test proving its requirement or labelled `qcthat-nocov`.
  [{qcthat}](https://github.com/Gilead-Public/qcthat) reports the
  issue-test matrix on every pull request and release.
- **Function Documentation** - Detailed documentation for each exported
  function with examples is maintained with Roxygen.
- **Package Checks** - Standard package checks are run using GitHub
  Actions and must be passing before PRs are merged.
- **Continuous Integration** - Continuous integration is provided via
  GitHub Actions.
- **Code Formatting** - Code is formatted with {styler} before each
  release.
- **Contributor Guidelines** - Detailed contributor guidelines including
  step-by-step processes for code development and releases are provided
  as a vignette.
- **Code Demonstration** -
  [Cookbook](https://impala-consortium.github.io/gsm.ctas/articles/Cookbook.html)
  Vignette provides demos and explanations for code usage.

### Parking

As development progresses, we will also conduct the following quality
control steps:

- **Qualification Workflow** - All assessments have been Qualified as
  described in the Qualification Workflow Vignette. A Qualification
  Report Vignette is generated and attached to each release.
- **Code Review** - Code review is conducted using GitHub Pull Requests
  (PRs), and a log of all PRs is included in the Qualification Report
  Vignette.
- **Data Specifications** - Machine-readable data specifications are
  maintained for all KRIs. Specifications are automatically added to
  relevant function documentation.
- **Regression Testing** - Extensive QC and testing is done before each
  release.
